Die warpage before and after the SMT process is expected, normal behavior.
Room-temperature die flatness is typically worse before SMT, and better (flatter) after SMT.
Die flatness post-SMT depends on all the same factors as package height post-SMT (Refer to the Section 4.4.1).

Die flatness post-SMT is particularly sensitive to motherboard thickness:
Thicker boards generally result in better die flatness (i.e., less curvature)

Awareness of die flatness post-SMT is important for proper heatsink design.
The heatsink pressure distribution on the Thermal Interface Material (TIM) and die can be measured using experimental. techniques described in Intel® Mobile SoC Die Loading Measurement Techniques (#556532).
For guidance on incorporating die flatness estimates into structural simulation during the heatsink mechanical design process, refer to Mobile Thermal Attach Structural Modeling (#575675).

For most accurate results, customers are strongly encouraged to measure die flatness post-SMT for their own particular board design and SMT process.
Values provided here are guidance only, for early thermal/mechanical design, and are not specifications.
